questionText:
Read the following riverine pollution and urban hydrology case study and answer the questions that follow:

The 22-kilometer stretch of the Yamuna River passing through the National Capital Territory of Delhi—from the Wazirabad barrage down to the Okhla barrage—accounts for less than 2% of the river's total length, yet contributes over 76% of the river's total pollution load. Upstream of Delhi, almost the entire fresh river flow is diverted at Hathnikund Barrage in Haryana for irrigation canals and municipal drinking water. As a result, the river enters Delhi at Wazirabad with virtually zero fresh environmental baseflow (E-flow) during non-monsoon months. Within Delhi, 22 major un-trapped municipal storm drains (including the infamous Najafgarh and Shahdara drains) discharge over 3,500 million liters per day (MLD) of untreated and partially treated sewage, industrial tanneries effluent, and chemical waste directly into the dry riverbed. During festival seasons, dramatic images of thick, white, toxic foam floating on the river at Kalindi Kunj and Okhla barrage make international headlines. Environmental chemists determined that the toxic frothing is caused by high concentrations of non-biodegradable surfactants from household detergents, industrial phosphate builders, and decaying organic matter. When wastewater plunges over the Okhla barrage gates, mechanical aeration and turbulence churn the surfactant-rich water into persistent, billowing foam containing pathogenic bacteria and heavy metals. Dissolved oxygen along this entire stretch remains at 0 mg/L throughout non-monsoon months, rendering the river ecologically dead.

Question: Under the Yamuna Action Plan and Namami Gange, what is the primary engineering strategy of 'Interception and Diversion' (I&D) projects?

options.text: Spraying chemical perfume into the open river to mask sewage smells
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Tapping open sewage drains before they reach the river and laying parallel interceptor trunk sewers to divert wastewater directly to modern Sewage Treatment Plants
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Interception and Diversion (I&D) Engineering Solution.

options.text: Building high concrete walls along the river so citizens cannot see the water
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Pumping polluted river water into private domestic swimming pools
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental Pollution (Interception and Diversion (I&D) Engineering Solution):
Tapping open sewage drains before they reach the river and laying parallel interceptor trunk sewers to divert wastewater directly to modern Sewage Treatment Plants

Detailed Context:
Interception & Diversion (I&D) captures sewage flowing through open storm drains, routing it through interceptor sewers to treatment plants before it hits the river.
Hence Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: In arid and semi-arid tracts of Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan, excessive flood irrigation from canals without adequate underground drainage leads to:

options.text: The complete elimination of all soil microbes within 5 minutes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Rapid cooling of the subsoil causing permanent permafrost formation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Instantaneous transformation of the soil into rich tropical volcanic peat
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Waterlogging followed by severe soil salinization (Reh / Kallar) as capillary action pulls dissolved mineral salts to the surface where water evaporates
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Soil Salinization in Canal-Irrigated Arid Lands.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Soil Salinization in Canal-Irrigated Arid Lands (Environmental Pollution):
Over-irrigation in poorly drained soils raises water tables; capillary action draws saline water upward, depositing white encrustations of sodium salts (salinization).
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: Unlike an open dump, an engineered 'Sanitary Landfill' prevents groundwater contamination and environmental hazards by incorporating:

options.text: Unlined porous sand pits that allow waste liquids to drain directly into aquifers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Open trenches situated directly inside floodplain wetlands
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

detailedSolution:

According to NCERT principles for Environmental Pollution (Sanitary Landfill Engineering Features):
An impermeable composite basal liner (compacted clay and HDPE geomembrane), a leachate collection and treatment system, and methane gas recovery vents

Sanitary landfills isolate waste using low-permeability clay liners (hydraulic conductivity < 10^-7 cm/s), synthetic HDPE geomembranes, leachate sumps, and methane wells.

topic: Soil Degradation Processes and Mitigating Conservation Practices
questionText:
Match the soil degradation hazard in List I with its standard conservation technique in List II:

List I:
(A) Slope runoff and water erosion
(B) Wind erosion in arid deserts
(C) Soil salinization and alkalinization
(D) Industrial heavy metal contamination

List II:
(I) Contour bunding and bench terracing
(II) Shelterbelts / Windbreaks of deep-rooted trees
(III) Application of agricultural gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) and sub-surface leaching drainage
(IV) Phytoremediation using hyperaccumulator plants (e.g., Brassica juncea)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Contour terracing curbs water runoff, shelterbelts stop wind erosion, gypsum rectifies sodic soils, and phytoremediation cleans heavy metals.
Hence Option D is correct.
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.

questionText:

Statement I: Oligotrophication is the reverse ecological process wherein a nutrient-rich lake transitions back toward a nutrient-poor, clear-water oligotrophic state.
Statement II: Diversion of sewage discharges, ban on phosphate detergents, and chemical precipitation with aluminum salts (alum) can induce oligotrophication.

Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
